text_blocks.snippet: HHS, or Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State, is a serious complication of diabetes, particularly type 2, characterized by extremely high blood sugar (hyperglycemia) and severe dehydration, leading to a very high concentration of blood (hyperosmolality), without significant ketoacidosis. It's diagnosed through blood tests showing severe hyperglycemia, hyperosmolality, and the absence of significant ketosis.
snippet_highlighted_words: blood tests showing severe hyperglycemia, hyperosmolality, and the absence of significant ketosis

list.title: Severe Hyperglycemia:
list.snippet: Blood sugar levels are very high, typically above 600 mg/dL (33.3 mmol/L).

list.title: Hyperosmolality:
list.snippet: The blood is very concentrated due to the high glucose levels and dehydration.

list.title: Dehydration:
list.snippet: Severe fluid loss due to osmotic diuresis (excessive urination caused by high glucose levels).

list.title: Lack of Significant Ketoacidosis:
list.snippet: Unlike DKA (another hyperglycemic emergency), HHS is characterized by the absence of significant ketone production in the body.

list.title: Neurological Symptoms:
list.snippet: Severe dehydration and hyperosmolality can affect brain function, leading to confusion, lethargy, and in severe cases, coma.

list.title: 1. Blood Glucose Test:
list.snippet: Measures the amount of glucose in the blood. In HHS, this level is significantly elevated, often above 600 mg/dL.

list.title: 2. Blood Osmolality Test:
list.snippet: Measures the concentration of dissolved particles in the blood. In HHS, this level is also elevated.

list.title: 3. Ketone Test:
list.snippet: Checks for the presence of ketones in the blood or urine. In HHS, ketone levels are typically low or absent.

list.title: 4. Other Tests:
list.snippet: May include blood gas analysis, electrolyte levels, and kidney function tests to assess overall health and rule out other conditions.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, the diagnosis of HHS hinges on identifying severe hyperglycemia and hyperosmolality in the absence of significant ketoacidosis.
